title: Quarter the optimizer batch (2^19 -> 2^17 tokens/step)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**17 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64, so grad_accum stays 1 and the run gets ~4x the optimizer steps in the same 5 minutes.
reflection: val_bpb 0.996458 vs baseline 0.997359, i.e. -0.0009: a real improvement but a small one. 3220 steps and 422.1M tokens (baseline sees roughly the same token count, so this is purely steps-vs-batch, not a token-budget change). MFU fell to 33.9% because per-step fixed overhead (Muon NS + AdamW over 67M of value-embedding params) is now amortized over 4x fewer tokens, and peak VRAM dropped to 22.7GB. Read: the batch axis is real but shallow here -- quartering the batch bought under a thousandth of a bpb, so the baseline 2^19 was only mildly oversized and I would not expect 2^16 to keep paying. The more interesting number is the VRAM and the MFU: at device batch 64 the optimizer-state and embedding cost dominates the step, which says the value embeddings (4 x 32768 x 512 = 67M params, larger than the entire transformer at 25M) are the real target for a future round, not the batch. I deliberately did not run 2^18 because a1 and a2 both proposed exactly that; the three results together should bracket the axis.
